title: CADMAGEDDON Agent Tops Frontier Models on Single GPU
summary: Moscow State University's open-source CADMAGEDDON agent runs on Qwen3.8-27B, beats Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra on CAD benchmarks using one 48 GB GPU.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Moscow State University released CADMAGEDDON, an open-source CAD reconstruction agent that runs locally on a single 48 GB GPU using Qwen3.8-27B.
- The system outperforms Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra on five benchmarks, achieving 0.991 IoU on BenchCAD versus 0.962 to 0.963 for frontier models.
- CADMAGEDDON splits reconstruction into visual decisions handled by the language model and numerical fitting done by geometric tools, integrating with FreeCAD.


Researchers from Moscow State University, Innopolis University, and FusionBrain Lab have released CADMAGEDDON, an open-source CAD reconstruction agent that runs locally on single-GPU systems and laptops using the mid-sized Qwen3.8-27B model. The system outperforms solutions built on frontier models across five major benchmarks while fitting on a single 48 GB GPU with FP8 weights. The preprint and code landed on GitHub on November 18, 2026.


## Officially launched on November 18, 2026


CADMAGEDDON became publicly available today through GitHub, with the research team releasing both the codebase and evaluation results. The system pairs the open-weight Qwen3.8-27B model with geometric fitting tools, enabling mesh-to-editable-CAD reconstruction on consumer hardware. The release includes integration with FreeCAD, allowing the agent to generate native FreeCAD programs and CadQuery output.


## Architecture splits vision from geometry


The design divides each reconstruction feature into two stages. A vision-language model selects the structure by choosing which plane, profile, and operation to apply. Geometric fitting supplies the numerical values. Algorithmic instruments detect planes, cross-sections, hole stacks, lines, and arcs, assign them short names, and the agent composes features by referring to those names. This separation allows the mid-sized language model to focus on structural decisions while delegating precision calculations to deterministic tools.


The authors report that the method assumes a clean mesh of a single part. Real scans and assemblies remain deferred work. A single reconstruction can require 30 to 60 model calls with long contexts, making it slower than single-pass learned models.


## Benchmark performance exceeds frontier models


On BenchCAD's 64³ voxel IoU metric, CADMAGEDDON scores 0.991 on a 1000-part subset. Vendor-reported entries for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, with tools), Claude Opus 5.5 (max, with tools), and GPT-6 Astra sit at 0.963, 0.962, and 0.959 on their 1000-part subsets, though the authors note that inputs and subsets differ.


On the MCB mechanical-parts benchmark, the system lifts IoU from CADFather's 0.862 to 0.933 and raises GMS, the metric comparing surface types, from 0.705 to 0.818 under the same evaluation. On CADENA-Bench, GMS jumps from 0.800 to 0.909. Task 3 of BenchCAD-2 sharpens the comparison: frontier models on the public leaderboard do not exceed a part score of 0.59, while CADMAGEDDON reaches 0.933 with CadQuery output and 0.925 with native FreeCAD programs at a reported $1.05 per part on OpenRouter pricing.


## Instruments carry accuracy, not scale


The same Qwen3.8-27B model wrapped in a general-purpose Qwen Code harness scores only 0.790 and returns no prediction on 2 of 23 parts in the BenchCAD-2 task. The authors conclude that the instruments, not model scale, carry much of the accuracy. This finding suggests that domain-specific tooling can enable mid-sized models to outperform larger frontier systems on specialized tasks.


- Runs on single 48 GB GPU with FP8 weights
- Integrates with FreeCAD for native program generation
- Open-source code available on GitHub
- Supports CadQuery and FreeCAD output formats


## Known limitations and failure cases


The research team states limits plainly. On BenchCAD-2, every attempt omits the 0.7 mm walls of one part and builds at most two of the 51 through-holes of another. The benchmarks are all CAD-derived, so the system's performance on real scans and assemblies remains unknown. The multi-call architecture creates longer inference times compared to single-pass approaches.


## What this means


CADMAGEDDON demonstrates that domain-specific tooling can enable mid-sized[open-source models](https://emergent.sh/glossary/open-source-model) to exceed frontier-model performance on specialized engineering tasks. By separating structural decisions from numerical fitting, the system achieves state-of-the-art results on five CAD benchmarks while running on consumer hardware. The local-first design and FreeCAD integration make the technology accessible to independent engineers and small shops without requiring API access or cloud infrastructure. The release arrives the same day as separate Qwen3.8-27B agent research, suggesting growing momentum around mid-sized models for specialized applications.
